title: Reduce the selected ADD/SCALE/COPY tape bill with a two-field cache
body:
The complete selected P104 scalar caller now retains frequently used fields in its existing two staging buffers. Each field has one authoritative copy; a cached field's owner slot is zero. Every acquisition, eviction, local circuit, rewind and SCALE/native/reset boundary flush is charged.

At W=64 the full scalar bill is **800,847,760 D − 5,118,198** for every positive payload dimension D. Relative to PR6527's complete owner-staging construction, it saves **435,314,176 D − 78,192** physical operations, about 35%, with no extra workspace: four tapes, 256D staging bits, one carry and two payload control bits. The same field-major owner backing and external boundary contracts remain.

The exact all-D optimum is restricted to the stated two-buffer no-prefetch policy: keep required resident fields, optimize bank assignment and all legal transfer orders, and flush before SCALE or external work. All 59,170 state rows and symbolic edge inequalities pass, with a single attaining path. No claim covers alternative circuits, retained SCALE, other layouts or weighted tariffs.

Evidence includes an independent exclusive-owner checker for every selected event; 37,715 actual scalar circuit calls with exact signed arithmetic at every prefix; 18,220,396 owner-record comparisons; and 94 literal physical windows covering all 43 templates, zero/one/two cache hits and all external boundary types. Those windows execute 25,987,056 metered operations and compare every owner/staging cell. Five controls reject bad potentials/totals, missing acquisition, incomplete flush and aliased tapes.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-exclusive-field-cache`.

The full scalar trace uses explicit native-grid and reset stubs. Native bodies, actual reset, initial layout construction, uniform encoded-D control, complete numerical/native admission, supplier funding and outer transfer remain open. The 7,936D bit-reset requests stay explicit and unimplemented. The all-D claim is a family of compiled W=64 schedules, not a uniform multiplication theorem or practical runtime measurement. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19365209). Canonical main, revision 8 and live overlap were refreshed. Exact predecessor bytes and original commits/paths/blobs/hashes are retained; no side-branch checkout is needed for replay. Credit PR6527/6513/6511, Nick Petalas, Sagar Thakrar / PR3241, DreamingOfClouds / PR6030 and the retained scalar/native/compiler lineage. Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
